It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Runs about 16 minutes; Tremendous, unhurried version; called one of the best of the 80s and the last second-set one known [27][34]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain is described as huge; Reviewer, sixth row, was blown away by the jamming in Scarlet, and Scarlet-Fire is cherished [31][33]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Opening Stranger is described as massive, one for the ages [31]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): Cold Rain and Snow in set one sounds especially thick and full on this recording [27]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Roses is a nice surprise in the first set [26]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Called the clear highlight, with Garcia's guitar playing wailing and intense [25]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): The crowd's roar at the opening notes of Dew is chill-inducing [26]
- **Day Job** (1 other source): Day Job is listed as the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-04-20.109353.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 159 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd84-04-20.senn.fishman.7854.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 168 min; rated 4.61/5 by 23 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording captures rumble of Phil's relatively new Modulus bass; sounds thick and full [27]
- **gd84-04-20.sbd.miller.27775.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the Miller FLAC soundboard crisp and says it replaced their first-generation audience tape [33]
- **gd84-04-20.sbd.clugston.11873.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 151 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: The Charlie Miller soundboard upgrade sounds crisp [31]
- **gd1984-04-20.166578.mtx.seamons.ht165.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 156 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [8]. Said about its sound: Soundboard speed slowed gradually in set one and was corrected; an 18-second patch in Fire On The Mountain was level-matched [8]
- **gd1984-04-20.154737.fob.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 154 min [9]
- **gd1984-04-20.149751.mke2002.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 19 songs; 160 min [15]

## Around the show

- The run had three shows at the Civic Center; reviewer got a friend's spare ticket for the 20th [29]
- Reviewer attended the whole tour, called this show one of the best but a little short [30]
- Venue was funky, dirty and old but felt small; UPenn hospital sits across the street [36]
- Reviewer thinks this run was the building's only attempt at hosting concerts; the balcony felt shaky [36]
- Pop Goes the Weasel was teased, and tape was stopped between songs to save tape [15]
- Reviewer is not a fan of 1984 but ranks this among that year's best shows [26]
- Reviewer prefers the soundboard copy of this show over the alternatives [30]
- Reviewer has heard better Morning Dews from 1984, citing the 4-14-84 Hampton show [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-04-20.109353.beyer-senn-daweez.D5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Beyer M160 and 1 Sennheiser 421 Microphones (14th row-center) > Nak MX100 w/2001 > Sony TCD5M (Dolby on) - analog master cassettes; [1]
- **gd84-04-20.senn.fishman.7854.sbeok.shnf**: source: Source Senn 441 > PCM Digital Audience (up-front) > DAT (SV3700) > DAT (Fostex D10) > CDR (Single WAV) >CDR-WAV (wav splits) > SHN (via MKWACT) [2]. Also: Audience taper is thought to have used Sennheiser 441 shotgun microphones [32]
- **gd84-04-20.sbd.miller.27775.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD> Cassette Master> Reel> Dat (SV3800/48k) [5]
- **gd84-04-20.sbd.clugston.11873.sbefail.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > CDR [7]
- **gd1984-04-20.166578.mtx.seamons.ht165.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) December 25, 2023 [8]. Also: Matrix uses Jeff Silberman's Sennheiser 441 DAT recording via Charlie Miller and Joe Noel to patch the soundboard [8]
- **gd1984-04-20.154737.fob.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes (section 102, row Y, seat 10); Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [9]
- **gd1984-04-20.149751.mke2002.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew: Sean Murtha; Tom Pinney; Kyle Holbrook; Gary Steel; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Source: MAUD CA: Sennheiser MKE2002 Binaurals mounted on dummy head 45 feet from stage ROC (13th row) >Sony TCD5M > TDK MA-R90s No Dolby - Master copy from… [15]

claims.text: Called the clear highlight, with Garcia's guitar playing wailing and intense
The crowd's roar at the opening notes of Dew is chill-inducing

claims.song: It Must Have Been The Roses
claims.text: Roses is a nice surprise in the first set
Reviewer is not a fan of 1984 but ranks this among that year's best shows
Audience recording captures rumble of Phil's relatively new Modulus bass; sounds thick and full
Runs about 16 minutes
Cold Rain and Snow in set one sounds especially thick and full on this recording
The run had three shows at the Civic Center; reviewer got a friend's spare ticket for the 20th
Reviewer attended the whole tour, called this show one of the best but a little short
Reviewer prefers the soundboard copy of this show over the alternatives
The Charlie Miller soundboard upgrade sounds crisp
Opening Stranger is described as massive, one for the ages
The Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain is described as huge
Audience taper is thought to have used Sennheiser 441 shotgun microphones
Reviewer calls the Miller FLAC soundboard crisp and says it replaced their first-generation audience tape
Reviewer, sixth row, was blown away by the jamming in Scarlet, and Scarlet-Fire is cherished
Reviewer has heard better Morning Dews from 1984, citing the 4-14-84 Hampton show
Tremendous, unhurried version; called one of the best of the 80s and the last second-set one known
Venue was funky, dirty and old but felt small; UPenn hospital sits across the street
Reviewer thinks this run was the building's only attempt at hosting concerts; the balcony felt shaky
Day Job is listed as the encore
Matrix uses Jeff Silberman's Sennheiser 441 DAT recording via Charlie Miller and Joe Noel to patch the soundboard
Soundboard speed slowed gradually in set one and was corrected; an 18-second patch in Fire On The Mountain was level-matched
Master is Doug Lamarre's FOB cassette, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Jeff Silberman's Sennheiser 441 patching short sections
Recorded with Sennheiser MKE2002 binaural microphones worn on a head or dummy head
Pop Goes the Weasel was teased, and tape was stopped between songs to save tape
